basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Cap. XXIII—Vers. 2.) Et mortua est Sara in civitate Arboc, quae est in valle: haec est'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXIII—Vers. 2.) Et mortua est Sara in civitate Arboc, quae est in valle: haec est Chebron, in terra Chanaan. Hoc quod hic positum est, quae est in valle, in authenticis codicibus non habetur. Nomen quoque civitatis Arboc paulatim a scribentibus legentibusque corruptum est. Neque enim putandum, Septuaginta Interpretes nomen civitatis Hebraeae, barbare atque corrupte, et aliter quam in suo dicitur, transtulisse. Arboc enim nihil omnino significat. Sed dicitur ARBEE (ארבע), hoc est, quatuor, quia ibi Abraham, et Isaac, et Jacob conditus est: et ipse princeps humani generis Adam, ut in Jesu libro apertius demonstrabitur.
